PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

minutes_text:
AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called meeting to order at 6:07 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE City Manager Hernandez led the Pledge of Allegiance. 

INVOCATION Councilmember Rebollo offered the invocation.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Proclamation Declaring October 23-31, 2024 as “Red Ribbon Week” in the City of Commerce Public Safety Manager Edson made a brief presentation, and Mayor Argumedo read the proclamation.  

PUBLIC COMMENT Honey Bizarro and Patricia Duares urged the City Council to engage more directly with the community.

Jasmin Gonzalez mentioned that several emails had been sent to the Council requesting a meeting, but the group had yet to receive a response.

In response, Mayor Argumedo directed staff to schedule a meeting to address the issues and concerns raised and work toward a resolution.

Mathew Lipson highlighted that his company previously used parking on Washington, but new signage prohibiting parking during peak hours was being installed. With 160 vehicles and insufficient space in the parking lot, this was creating challenges.

Chris Griego expressed gratitude to the City Council for their support of the football camp.

Gloria Nezahualcoyotl raised concerns about the social club at the senior center, urging that a fair election be conducted for officers and that the rules and by-laws be enforced. Mayor Argumedo acknowledged the issue, stating that the by-laws were outdated and would be revised following the election.





CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo

3.. Approval of Minutes

7.. Agreement with Sky Elements Drone Show, Inc. for the City Birthday Opening Ceremonies  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz provided a brief overview of the staff report.  

4.. Allocating Funds for Annual 2025 Commerce Calendars

5.. Council Meeting Schedule - Cancellation of November 26, 2024 and December 24, 2024 Meetings Due to Upcoming Holidays and Anticipated Lack of Business

2.. Approval of Warrant Register No. 7A

SCHEDULED MATTERS

6.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Duarte provided a summary of crime statistics from the past two weeks and gave an update on the FLOCK License Plate Reader system. She highlighted the system's benefits in helping prevent and solve certain crimes.

Councilmember Lainez inquired about the date range covered in the report. Sergeant Duarte explained that the FLOCK system retains information for 30 days. 
When asked by Councilmember Lainez about the meaning of a "hotlist," Sergeant Duarte clarified that it refers to vehicles either reported as stolen or those they are trying to identify in connection with crimes in the area.

Councilmember Lainez also asked how frequently the Sheriff's Department assesses strategies to prevent crime, specifically emphasizing the high rates of property crime. Sergeant Duarte responded that most crimes occur at the Shopping Center and Citadel Outlets. She mentioned that they have met with the management of the Shopping Center, and there are plans to install additional parking lot cameras to help deter criminal activity.

Sergeant Duarte commended Citadel for their efforts, noting that they have assigned deputies and security personnel to the area. She also recommended that residents and visitors take precautions, such as not leaving valuables in their trunks or cars.

Mayor Argumedo reported suspicious activity occurring behind homes in the area near Jack in the Box and requested an evaluation of how to enhance patrol efforts in that vicinity. He also noted multiple accidents at the intersection of Slauson and Greenwood and asked the City Manager to investigate safety improvements for that intersection.


8.. Rental of Security Camera Trailers for a 12-Month Period  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Public Safety Manager Edson provided an overview of the staff report regarding the mobile cameras. Councilmember Garcia expressed appreciation for the introduction of another crime prevention strategy but raised concerns about the potential misuse of the mobile cameras. Councilmember Garcia inquired if there were any risks of these cameras being misused. Manager Edson clarified that the cameras would be placed only on public property, such as parks and industrial areas at night, and not on private property. He further explained that only Deputies, public safety staff, and City Mnaager, if requested, would have access to the footage. Councilmember Garcia also voiced concern about potential penalties if the trailers housing the cameras were not set up properly. Manager Edson reassured her that only trained staff members would handle the setup, ensuring it would be done correctly.



ORDINANCES

9.. Adoption and Second Reading of an Ordinance to Approve Development Agreement Related to Commercial Cannabis Permit Application No. 18-026 for Commercial Cannabis Testing  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano

10.. Adoption and Second Reading of an Ordinance to Approve Development Agreement Related to Commercial Cannabis Permit Application No. 18-047  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia reported attending the 2024 Service Education Award event at the Montebello Unified School District, and congratulated Mr. Whitmore for being recognized for his significant contributions.

Councilmember Rebollo congratulated the sports teams currently traveling and thanked the Veterans Park community for their patience as the much-needed remediation project begins. She emphasized the importance of the upcoming national election and encouraged residents to vote. Councilmember Rebollo also expressed her gratitude to the Library Department for hosting the "Pizza and Politics" workshops, which she believes are vital for educating the community on ballot measures and the voting process.

Councilmember Lainez shared that he attended a "Thriving Communities" meeting at the Department of Transportation hosted by the COG. The focus was on improving connectivity in the I-710 corridor. The program provided technical assistance for grant writing and project scoping. Councilmember Lainez met representatives from the Federal Railroad Administration, and talked with them about accident years ago in Commerce and that the railroad safety wall buffer was never completed. FRA representatives noted that there are a couple of grant opportunities available through the Federal Railroad Administration to address this issue.

Vice Mayor Altamirano discussed his recent meeting with the Tax Assessor’s office to discuss concerns that were raised by residents about property taxes when passing homes to their children. Vice Mayor Altamirano informed that there is a form that can be completed to maintain a low tax base when a home is inherited. Vice Mayor Altamirano also mentioned an upcoming presentation on this topic. Additionally, Vice Mayor Altamirano noted that some residents have reported their home insurance being canceled or significantly increased. Vice Mayor Altamirano requested the City Manager to reach out to the Insurance Commissioner to investigate the matter. Lastly, Vice Mayor wished good luck to all candidates running for office.

Mayor Argumedo also attended the Friends of Montebello Unified District Foundation Service Award event and congratulated Mr. Whitmore on his recognition.


ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 7:30 pm
